idiom_name: legacy-shaped DTO structs + small interface adapters
implementation_notes: Go windows are ordinary types: declare request and response structs that carry the legacy JSON tags (or a MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON pair when tags cannot express the old encoding) and convert explicitly into the domain types, keeping the old names out of the new core. Because interfaces are satisfied structurally, the window implements the legacy interface simply by having the methods - no declaration, no inheritance - so a thin adapter type over the core is the whole structure. Hand-written mapping is still justified when the legacy shape encodes semantics that tags cannot express (implicit defaults, unit codes, zero values that mean 'absent'), which is the normal case for old protocols.
pitfalls: Legacy JSON that distinguishes null from absent needs pointer fields or a custom UnmarshalJSON; plain value fields collapse both into the zero value.
empty is not omitted in the old shape: nil slices marshal to null while empty slices marshal to [], and omitempty changes which of the two the client sees.
Wrapping errors with %w changes the message an old client may be parsing; map to the legacy text and code explicitly at the boundary.
